title: Three Gates Open at Once
text:
Sigrun Veyrhald opened three gates at once.

The western gate sent riders against Rui’s supply road. The eastern opened around Mo’s imperial centre. The central shield line descended toward Lei’s mobile wing. Each attack carried enough banners to look decisive, and every signal reached Jin at a different speed.

By the time the third lantern arrived, Kael was already moving.

Sigrun met him beneath the First Banner with a shield taller than her shoulder. No announcement named her. The Veyrhald lines simply changed around her until seventy thousand soldiers treated one woman as the place the centre began.

Kael released **Nine Heavens Collapse**.

The first strike broke the outer shield layer. The second folded the ground beneath it. The third drove three hundred Veyrhald soldiers backward without breaking their formation.

Sigrun received every impact through **The First Wall Outlives the Siege**.

The force did not vanish. Surviving it became memory inside the next defence. When Kael’s fourth strike descended, the shield line stood heavier than the first.

He felt the difference through his weapon.

[[speaker:sigrun]]“Again,” Sigrun said.

Kael did not mistake invitation for confidence. She wanted his strength committed where her law could learn its weight.

Behind him, three casualty reports contradicted one another. One claimed the western supply line had fallen. Another placed Dravaryn cavalry inside Mo’s rear. The third named three Hearth settlements trapped beyond Sigrun’s central gate.

Jin reached Kael before the next strike.

[[speaker:jin]]“The gate wants you.”

[[speaker:kael]]“The names?”

[[speaker:jin]]“Real settlements. Unconfirmed condition.”

Sigrun withdrew one shield layer. Too cleanly. A narrow road opened toward the Hearths while every other route around Kael became harder.

[[speaker:jin]]“If you enter, she decides where the Mountain stands.”

Kael looked beyond the opening. Smoke rose from one settlement. It might be signal smoke. People might still be beneath it.

[[speaker:kael]]“Then keep the army from following me.”

He entered alone.

Sigrun let him pass without turning her shield.

Across Three-Gate Plain, the western and eastern attacks changed direction at the same moment. The gates had never been separate. They had been three hands closing around Wuyue’s divided response.

title: Stormreach Breaks the False Gate
text:
Lei destroyed the western gate before Isgard finished pretending it was real.

Stormreach thunderfire crossed the fortification joints in six synchronized bursts. Engineers shattered hinge stones. Fast infantry entered through the opening while cavalry circled the wall instead of crowding the breach.

The first courtyard held abandoned cooking fires. The second contained broken wagons arranged to look hastily left behind. Beyond the third waited an exposed supply column retreating north beneath imperfect cover.

Stormreach officers saw victory trying to escape.

“Cavalry forward!”

Lei raised one hand.

[[speaker:lei]]“Hold.”

The word travelled unevenly. The front companies stopped. Two rear cohorts continued through the gate before signal riders reached them. Isgard scouts scattered in convincing panic, dropping food sacks and one command map marked with a route toward the central army.

Lei knelt beside the nearest sack. The grain inside was dry despite three days of rain.

The retreat had been packed for discovery.

[[speaker:lei]]“Supply depth?”

His quartermaster unfolded the latest road count.

“Rui’s nearest secure convoy is seventeen miles south. If we pursue, the cavalry reaches the marked column before sunset. The infantry does not.”

“Enemy riders?”

“Moving toward the road we leave behind.”

Stormreach could destroy the visible wagons and return hungry, separated and proud. A younger Lei would already have been thunder on the northern road.

He ordered the broken gate dismantled for stone and timber. Cavalry screened the engineers instead of chasing scouts. The two advanced cohorts returned angry and alive.

One captain placed the captured map before him.

“They will say we lost our nerve.”

[[speaker:lei]]“They built us a victory that required no enemy to defend it.”

Lei burned the map without opening the final fold.

Before midnight, Isgard riders struck the supply road Stormreach had almost abandoned. They found cavalry waiting behind fortification stone carried from the false gate.

The gate fell.

The army behind it remained connected to its food.

title: The Imperial Army Holds Its First Foreign Line
text:
Raska’s cavalry and Eldran’s armoured infantry struck Mo’s centre as one front.

The cavalry arrived first beneath red pennants, but its attack did not seek a breakthrough. **Crimson Cavalry Crosses the Setting Sun** carried the completed momentum of one charge into the next. Each withdrawal preserved force instead of spending it. The imperial shield line bent farther every time Raska returned.

Behind her, Eldran planted a blackened standard into ground his infantry had already crossed.

**Cinder Standard Over the Fallen Mile** answered through the road. Heat and armoured pressure travelled beneath Mo’s forward companies. Boots lost purchase. Formation weight shifted toward the western turn Raska had prepared.

Jin saw the shape from the ridge.

[[speaker:jin]]“Refuse the west. Sacrifice the forward formation.”

Mo’s paper-command layers were already burning.

The outer orders had directed fifty-two thousand soldiers toward the original line. When Raska broke that shape, the damaged pages opened instructions hidden beneath them. Brigades changed direction without waiting for one messenger to cross the entire army.

[[speaker:mo]]“Third and seventh fold inward. Royal Guard holds no special centre.”

Jin turned.

[[speaker:jin]]“I ordered the western line refused.”

[[speaker:mo]]“There are two Hearth villages behind the eastern fold. Your ridge cannot see them.”

The correction cost the imperial army ground. Raska broke the forward line and found another behind it, angled away from the road she intended to capture. Eldran’s stored mile released beneath the abandoned position instead of the civilians.

Royal Guard soldiers fought among ordinary brigades. No protected centre told Dravaryn where the regency seal stood. Mo moved twice before the enemy located his first paper shelter.

Raska charged a third time. Imperial spears received less force because she had been made to turn across ground Eldran did not own. The line still broke in two places. Paper riders carried local authority into both gaps before Mo could speak.

At sunset, the imperial army stood three miles behind its opening position.

It stood intact.

Jin looked from the preserved villages to the line he had intended to spend.

[[speaker:jin]]“You changed my order.”

[[speaker:mo]]“I corrected for citizens you could not see.”

Their partnership survived its first foreign battle because number three did not require being obeyed more than he required the army to remain alive.

title: Arin Cuts Only the Siege
text:
Isgard siege engines entered the imperial flank behind Raska’s fourth charge.

They moved on linked iron frames, each machine protecting the joints of the next. Breaking one carelessly would collapse burning weight into Mo’s retreating infantry. Leaving them intact would let the engines close the only road wide enough for the wounded.

Kael held the pressure that would have crushed the space around them. Sigrun’s shield lines pressed him from the north while three thousand Silver Horizon swordswomen entered the machinery below.

Arin divided the sect by function. Field disciples marked crew exits. Inner disciples cut command ropes. Senior matrons held falling armour plates long enough for trapped engineers to crawl free.

**When the Silver Horizon Breaks** crossed the first engine line.

Every locking joint opened in one silver interval. The machines remained standing for half a breath, separated without yet knowing they had become pieces.

An Isgard engineer dropped his hammer and raised both hands. A young inner disciple saw the formation seal at his belt and lifted her sword.

[[speaker:arin]]“The siege. Not the hands.”

“He can rebuild it.”

[[speaker:arin]]“So can the person you kill beside him.”

The disciple changed angle and shattered the final control pin. The engineer pulled two crew members through the gap before the frame collapsed.

On the northern edge, Kael found an opening wide enough to destroy the remaining engines and everyone between them. He looked down once.

Arin pointed her sword toward three narrow seams.

Kael followed those seams. His force broke iron where she had already cleared bodies. He did not widen the strike because greater power was available.

Former master and student moved as separate commanders serving one purpose.

The last engine crew surrendered after their command ropes fell. Silver Horizon disciples bound weapons, opened treatment lanes and rotated their own wounded out before pursuing anyone.

The siege collapsed without becoming a grave for the people forced to operate it.

Above the wreckage, Sigrun’s line withdrew again.

Arin watched it go and understood that saving the crews had cost time the First Wall intended to use elsewhere. Mercy had not been free.

She ordered the sect forward anyway.

title: Skeldran Hunts the Hospital
text:
Solveig Skeldran found Yun’s antidote route beneath three false trails.

One genuine footprint had crossed the snow beside a medicine cart. **No Footprint Survives the Last Snow** propagated from that contact through every later concealment. False paths did not confuse the pursuit. They became proof that something had chosen to hide.

Skeldran Hunt companies closed from four directions.

Varok reached the southern ridge and saw the white Eirholt stakes below. Patients filled the road between them: Isgard infantry, Wuyue sailors, burned engine crews and three children from the nearest Hearth.

[[speaker:varok]]“The target is inside a medical corridor.”

Solveig did not slow.

[[speaker:solveig]]“Wuyue hides military movement beneath physicians.”

[[speaker:varok]]“Duskvein used medicine as bait.”

[[speaker:solveig]]“And Wuyue crossed with an army.”

Both accusations carried evidence. Neither changed the bodies on the road.

Beyond the basin, Liang pressed two fingers into the snow. She could not erase the genuine trail without confirming where it ended. Yun opened her medicine ledger instead.

[[speaker:yun]]“Give her routes that remain true.”

Liang looked at her.

[[speaker:yun]]“Heat patterns. Carrying rhythm. Antidote residue. Nothing taken from a patient.”

They sent harmless circulation signatures into six empty medicine sleds. Each became a plausible team moving away from the white road. Solveig’s art accepted them because Yun had not constructed illusions; real antidote heat travelled along real runners.

The Hunt divided.

Solveig followed the original trace toward the basin. Varok withheld two companies and placed them across the approach—not against Wuyue, but between Skeldran arrows and the patients below.

Solveig stopped within sight of the white stakes.

[[speaker:solveig]]“Move.”

[[speaker:varok]]“Not through Eirholt.”

Behind them, four false medicine teams crossed separate ridges. The remaining Hunt companies had to choose which trails represented military escape.

Eira closed the corridor after the final litter entered and wrote down every banner that had approached it armed.

Skeldran did not become Wuyue’s ally. Its disagreement bought the hospitals twenty-three minutes.

On a battlefield measured in armies, twenty-three minutes moved twelve hundred wounded people beyond the Hunt.

title: Luo Wen Buries No Patient Early
text:
Luo built three casualty stations and gave none a ranking entrance.

The first occupied an abandoned grain yard. The second moved beneath Rui’s temporary ice roofs. The third existed only as red lanterns carried by physicians who expected the line to change before the wounded arrived.

A Marquis waited behind a soldier whose airway had collapsed beneath shield pressure. A Silver Horizon matron waited behind an Isgard cook burned inside a siege engine. The Marquis’s aide placed a rank seal on Luo’s table.

Luo set a bloodied instrument on top of it.

[[speaker:luo]]“Cultivation changes treatment. It does not purchase time from the person dying beside you.”

The outer warning bell rang before the aide found an answer.

Isgard pressure had closed around the grain yard. Lei reached the station with meridians already strained from breaking the false gate.

[[speaker:lei]]“How many cannot walk?”

“Three hundred fourteen. Seventy cannot survive ordinary transport.”

Lei looked at the distance to the second station.

He began moving groups through thunderfire. Physicians crossed first with instruments and blood stores. Critical litters followed inside brief channels where motion became one protected burst. Every crossing reopened heat damage along Lei’s legs.

A wounded commander caught his sleeve.

“Take me on the next passage.”

[[speaker:lei]]“Can you walk?”

“I am a field general.”

[[speaker:lei]]“That was not the question.”

The man stood.

[[speaker:lei]]“Then you are behind the people who cannot.”

He released the sleeve.

At the second station, Luo treated the airway, then the cook, then the Marquis whose cultivation had kept his bleeding slow enough to wait. The aide found his rank seal cleaned and placed beside the discharge route.

The grain yard fell after the final physicians left. Isgard captured empty tables, bloodied cloth and one broken lantern.

All three casualty stations survived by refusing to become buildings worth defending.

No patient was buried early merely because someone stronger wanted the bed.

title: Ilyra Returns What the Host Receives
text:
The imperial flank collapsed toward Rui’s frozen escape road.

Eldran’s stored ground broke the wagons first. Raska’s cavalry pressure followed through the gap before Mo’s paper orders could rebuild it. Thousands moved toward a road narrow enough that panic would kill more people than the charge.

Ilyra placed Shield Wing between the retreat and Dravaryn.

One meridian system received the impact. Eight thousand Crownless soldiers became layers around it, each taking only the force their formation could pass without breaking. Ilyra’s second system opened beneath the first.

[[speaker:ilyra]]“Receive on three.”

Raska’s charge landed.

Shield Wing bent. Soldiers in the outer rank lost footing and were caught by the rank behind them. Pressure travelled through Ilyra’s divided circulation into Returning Wing.

[[speaker:ilyra]]“Return on five.”

The stored force could have gone back through the cavalry. Instead Ilyra released it sideways. Ground, shattered wagons and Isgard pressure moved away from Rui’s road. A corridor opened without one returning strike pursuing the riders who had created it.

Rui changed ice beneath the retreating formations. Broken carts floated across surfaces that became water after they passed. Soldiers who fell did not strike stone; the current carried them toward imperial hands waiting downstream.

An imperial captain pointed at Raska’s exposed rear.

“We can countercharge.”

[[speaker:ilyra]]“Nobody chases.”

“They will reform.”

[[speaker:ilyra]]“So will the people behind you if you keep the road open.”

The Crownless Host spent the force of a cavalry assault on space. Rui spent control of water on people rather than drowning the formation that had attacked them.

The last imperial wagon crossed. Returning Wing released its remaining pressure into empty ground and withdrew before Dravaryn’s next charge arrived.

Thousands escaped through a road made from one army’s defence and another Sovereign’s river.

From the red grasslands, Eldran watched the partnership complete.

Isgard had found two systems it would later need to separate.

title: Kael Holds the Centre Alone
text:
Kael stopped Veyrhald’s heavy formation without one Stonecrown soldier behind him.

**The Mountain Does Not Move** fixed the centre. Shield waves struck his position and divided around it. Ground split behind his heels. Every soldier within the protected angle remained standing.

Sigrun received him at the boundary she had chosen.

Kael broke three shields. The Veyrhald line replaced them without advancing. He broke the stone beneath Sigrun’s feet. **The First Wall Outlives the Siege** remembered the earlier impacts and made the accepted ground heavier.

He could destroy more of the formation. He could not move the woman whose Supreme art had made surviving him part of the next defence.

Sigrun looked toward the southern smoke.

[[speaker:sigrun]]“A settlement beyond the east road sent a civilian bell.”

Kael did not turn.

[[speaker:sigrun]]“You heard it,” she said.

[[speaker:kael]]“So did you.”

[[speaker:sigrun]]“I know which army occupies the road between.”

The bell rang again, distant and irregular.

Kael held the centre. Jin’s formation depended on him remaining. Somewhere beyond Sigrun’s wall, the bell could be bait or people could be dying while two Sovereigns demonstrated discipline.

Sigrun learned from the pause. Names could move Kael where force could not.

In Wuyue, Tae stood alone against Huo and Qin around the marked village objective. Huo’s nine Wheels attacked the body. Qin’s vibration map attacked every route. Tae denied both approaches and discovered the western evacuation had moved beyond the distance he was protecting.

Quiet Hand observers marked the failure.

Tae had held the centre and lost the people leaving it.

Across two continents, neither battlefield offered a clean lesson. Kael remained where the army needed him and heard the bell a third time. Tae abandoned one perfect anchor to recover the simulated civilians he had stopped seeing.

Holding a centre was not the same as protecting everything that gave the centre meaning.

Sigrun lowered her shield by one inch.

The bell stopped.

Kael did not know whether that meant rescue or silence.

title: Liang Finds Two Circulations in One War
text:
Liang heard two command rhythms beneath Isgard’s ordinary signals.

The first belonged to Halvek Veyrhald’s sealed military roads. Gates opened, redirected and compressed movement without Halvek appearing personally. A formation fifty miles away could be made to arrive as reinforcement or discover the road beneath it had become a wall.

The second rhythm ran deeper.

It did not resemble an army. It resembled one martial law waiting for a complete body.

[[speaker:liang]]“Paragon inheritance.”

Three roads closed around her.

[[speaker:halvek]]Halvek’s voice travelled through the nearest gate seal. “White Blood hears what it enters. These roads are not your body.”

Liang placed one finger against the stone.

[[speaker:liang]]“Everything carrying force has circulation.”

She released **White Blood: Vein Whisper** into the first seal. Halvek treated the road as external structure and reinforced it from another junction. The dormant fragment travelled with that reinforcement before becoming still.

The second road contracted. Liang sent a false team down it and let the gate close completely around empty movement. The third held her prepared medical cache and two months of antidote stock.

Yun’s voice came through the retreat signal.

[[speaker:yun]]“Leave it.”

Liang watched white medicine cases disappear behind Veyrhald stone.

[[speaker:liang]]“I know.”

Knowing did not make the loss abstract. Yun would have to divide remaining antidotes. Patients would receive narrower margins because Liang had chosen to preserve the seed inside Halvek’s road instead of the cache.

She escaped through the route created when the false team forced two gates to share one command pulse. Halvek sealed it behind her before the last thread of her robe cleared.

The roads remained closed.

Liang had lost ground, medicine and every obvious path toward Halvek’s body. Inside the seals, White Blood waited where he believed no body existed.

Far beneath both rhythms, the incomplete Paragon inheritance continued circulating.

Liang heard it once more before distance erased the sound.

title: The First Gate Was the Road Behind Them
text:
The first summer uniforms had been repaired into autumn ones by the time Jin found the true gate.

Black campaign strips faded beneath rain and smoke. Soldiers who had arrived calling every northern ridge foreign now gave directions by burned mills, rebuilt bridges and the names of Hearth families selling grain. Letters from Wuyue took six weeks to reach the front. Some arrived for people already buried.

Throughout those months, Isgard had not tried to destroy Wuyue’s forward army.

It had been closing the route behind it.

Jin placed burned supply markers beside Halvek’s road seals and Solveig’s patrol reports. Together they formed one boundary from the inland campaign back to the Black Current.

[[speaker:jin]]“The first gate was behind us.”

Mo followed the line with one finger.

[[speaker:mo]]“If it closes?”

[[speaker:jin]]“We become an army living from territory that does not want us here.”

Rui moved before the council finished. He found inland water channels too narrow for transports and froze them into one continuous southern corridor. The new road could carry supplies and wounded, not the complete expedition. Every mile required engineers to keep water pressure from breaking through beneath loaded carts.

Isgard attacked the first convoy before sunset.

Rui held the ice while Stormreach guarded its edges. Grain reached the army. Three wagons did not. The route existed, thin enough that every future delivery would remain a battle.

Late in the same year, Huo stood alone against Tae and Qin around the marked village in Wuyue.

Tae denied every approach he recognized. Qin transmitted pressure through routes Huo had already adapted to once. The nine Meridian Wheels changed answer after answer until Huo stopped commanding them separately.

Adaptation itself became the stable centre.

One Wheel received Tae’s compressed distance and gave its force to movement. Another changed Qin’s vibration into reinforcement. The remaining seven exchanged purpose without waiting for damage to tell them what they were allowed to become.

Peak Sovereign pressure settled across the field.

Huo could have struck either opponent. Instead he closed the final road toward the marked civilians and held it while both attacks completed.

Quiet Hand physicians called the field safe.

Huo lowered his Wheels without celebration.

The first of Wuyue’s three hidden guardians had reached the summit.

North of him, Rui’s narrow ice road carried the Black March through the gate Isgard had tried to close behind it.
